locator: VII, lect. 2 n. 893: it is not an efficacious proof
interpretation: Aquinas agrees with Aristotle that the first argument does not conclude: an infinite motion in finite time is possible when it is the many motions of infinitely many different mobiles. Read as the same proposition as Aristotle's claim ARIST-PHYS-242B19-INITIAL-REDUCTIO-FAILS-A: the simultaneous-motion reductio alone does not show that the series has a first member. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
